description:
Decision gate from the 2026-07-12 tuning-system deep review (evidence pinned to
commit acfb8992; findings C4-C6).

Decisions needed before mode/facet implementation work:

1. FALLBACK LABELING. `--tuning tuned` with no template silently runs a bare
   default config still labeled "tuned" (benchbox/cli/tuning_resolver.py:295-307,
   benchbox/cli/commands/run.py:1016-1022) and facet-matches curated-template
   runs. Options: keep, introduce a distinct mode (e.g. tuned-fallback /
   constraints), or refuse in non-interactive / --official runs.
2. MODE VOCABULARY PIN. Python emits tuned/notuning/auto/<raw path> plus
   "balanced" (benchbox/cli/tuning.py:52,56); the explorer knows
   tuned/notuning/auto and defaults missing to "untuned"
   (results-explorer/src/lib/facetMatching.ts:99). Decide the canonical value
   set, whether raw file paths are a legal mode value (they leak local paths into
   bundles), and how absent-vs-baseline must be distinguished.
3. CROSS-PLATFORM "TUNED" FACET. Platform X tuned may render 6 physical
   mechanisms while platform Y renders zero; the facet matches them. Decide
   whether facet matching stays mode-string-based, incorporates
   physical_rendering_id / mechanism counts, or adds a receipt-level warning.

work_units.notes:
Joe adopted the recommended defaults on 2026-07-12. Decision recorded in
docs/development/tuning-adr-002-mode-vocabulary-fallback-facets.md:

1. FALLBACK LABELING: a `--tuning tuned` run with no template gets the
   distinct mode value `tuned-fallback` (not `tuned`), and is refused under
   `--official`. Wizard-produced configs get source provenance `wizard`.
2. VOCABULARY PIN: canonical tuning_mode values are exactly `tuned`,
   `tuned-fallback`, `notuning`, `auto`, `custom`. Raw file paths are not
   legal mode values; custom-file runs emit `custom` + a template
   ref/hash. The wizard's `balanced` string maps into this set as a
   template flavor, not a mode. Absent/unrecorded is a distinct
   "not recorded" state in ingest and UI, never coerced to `notuning`.
   The vocabulary lives in one shared artifact consumed by both Python
   and TypeScript test suites.
3. FACET RULE: tuning_mode stays the coarse comparability facet with
   exact-match semantics over the pinned vocabulary; ComparabilityReceipt
   warns when two "tuned" runs have disjoint physical mechanism sets;
   physical_rendering_id becomes a secondary matchable facet for TPC
   benchmarks. Unknown/not-recorded never silently matches `notuning`.

Implementation is deferred to tuning-mode-vocabulary-and-facet-implementation-20260712,
tuning-explorer-ingest-mode-extraction-20260712, and
tuning-soundness-test-coverage-20260712.
